prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A collapsible and expandable stent body includes a generally tubular annulus section, one or more prosthetic valve elements mounted to the stent body, and a cuff attached to the stent body. The prosthetic valve is operative to allow flow in an antegrade direction but to substantially block flow in a retrograde direction. The prosthetic heart valve may include paravalvular leak mitigation features in the form of first and second sealing members. The sealing members are attached to the cuff and extend circumferentially around an abluminal surface of the stent body. The sealing members each have an open side facing in a first axial direction and a closed side facing in an opposite second axial direction. Flow of blood in the second axial direction will tend to force blood into the sealing members and cause the sealing members to billow outwardly relative to the stent body, helping to mitigate paravalvular leak.

The collapsible and expandable stent body includes a generally tubular annular section, one or more prosthetic valve elements, and a cuff attached to the stent body. The prosthetic valve elements are configured to permit blood flow through the stent body in an antegrade direction while substantially preventing flow in the retrograde direction.

To mitigate paravalvular leakage, first and second sealing members are attached to the cuff and arranged around the abluminal surface of the stent body. Each sealing member includes an open side facing one axial direction and a closed side facing the opposite axial direction. A collapsible and expandable prosthetic heart valve is configured for minimally invasive delivery to a native valve site. The prosthesis includes a generally tubular stent that can be compressed for insertion through a catheter and expanded at the implantation site. One or more flexible valve elements are mounted within the stent to permit blood flow in the forward direction while restricting reverse flow. A cuff disposed around at least part of the stent provides a supporting interface between the prosthesis and the surrounding native tissue.

The prosthesis further includes circumferential sealing members arranged around the exterior of the stent. These sealing members form flexible pockets or cavities capable of receiving blood that flows in a retrograde direction. When reverse pressure develops, the captured blood causes the sealing members to billow or deflect outwardly toward the adjacent tissue. This outward expansion allows the seals to conform to irregularities in the native annulus and occupy spaces between the stent and the surrounding anatomy.

By dynamically closing such gaps, the sealing members reduce the amount of blood that can pass around, rather than through, the prosthetic valve. The design therefore limits paravalvular leakage without requiring excessive radial force from the stent. It can also accommodate variations in patient anatomy and changes in loading during the cardiac cycle, improving sealing, hemodynamic performance, and the overall function of the implanted valve.

The flow is the quiet rhythm that carries life forward. It moves through rivers, conversations, ideas, and time itself. We often resist it, trying to control every turn, but the flow cannot be held for long.

To follow the flow is not to surrender without purpose. It is to pay attention—to recognize when to act, when to wait, and when to let go. Like water finding its path around stone, we can move through challenges with patience and persistence.

The flow reminds us that change is constant. Nothing remains still, yet every ending creates space for something new. When we trust the movement of life, uncertainty becomes less frightening, and each moment becomes part of a larger journey.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a prosthetic heart valve with a collapsible stent body and sealing members designed to reduce paravalvular leakage.
counterfactuals.output:
A prosthetic heart valve may include a radially collapsible and expandable stent body configured for catheter-based delivery and deployment within a native valve annulus. The stent body supports a valve assembly having flexible leaflets that permit forward blood flow and inhibit reverse flow.

One or more sealing members are positioned around the exterior of the stent body. These may include:

- an annular fabric or polymer skirt covering gaps between the stent struts;
- compressible cuffs, pads, or lobes that conform to irregular anatomy;
- expandable pockets that fill with blood or sealing material after deployment; and/or
- overlapping inner and outer skirts that create a tortuous leakage path.

When the stent expands, the sealing members are pressed against the native annulus and surrounding tissue, filling calcification-related voids and other gaps between the prosthesis and the anatomy. This improves circumferential sealing and reduces paravalvular leakage while allowing the valve to remain collapsible for transcatheter delivery.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a transcatheter heart valve featuring circumferential cuffs that billow outward when exposed to retrograde blood flow.
counterfactuals.output: A prosthetic heart valve for transcatheter implantation includes an expandable annular frame, a plurality of valve leaflets supported within the frame, and one or more circumferential cuffs coupled to an exterior portion of the frame. Each cuff comprises a flexible membrane defining an annular pocket having an opening oriented to receive retrograde blood flow. Upon exposure to retrograde flow, blood enters the pocket and causes the cuff to billow radially outward into engagement with surrounding native tissue, thereby sealing paravalvular gaps and reducing regurgitation. During antegrade flow, the cuff may at least partially collapse toward the frame to reduce obstruction to blood flow. The cuff may include multiple circumferential segments, compliant folds, or porous regions configured to accommodate irregular anatomy and promote tissue ingrowth. The prosthetic valve is compressible for delivery through a catheter and expandable at a target cardiac valve site.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain how first and second sealing members attached to the cuff of an expandable prosthetic valve can mitigate paravalvular leak.
counterfactuals.output:
First and second sealing members attached to the cuff of an expandable prosthetic valve can reduce **paravalvular leak (PVL)** by creating multiple barriers between the valve frame and the irregular native anatomy.

- **Conform to gaps:** When the valve expands, the sealing members are compressed against the native annulus, leaflets, or vessel wall. Their compliant material fills spaces caused by calcification, uneven tissue, or imperfect valve sizing.
- **Provide seals at different locations:** The members may be positioned at different axial or circumferential regions of the cuff. If blood passes the first seal, the second seal provides an additional barrier before it can travel around the valve.
- **Interrupt leak pathways:** Offset, overlapping, or differently shaped sealing members create a longer, more tortuous flow path, increasing resistance to blood flow outside the prosthetic valve.
- **Accommodate movement and recoil:** Two sealing elements can maintain contact despite frame recoil, cardiac motion, or local variations in contact pressure.
- **Promote longer-term sealing:** If made from porous, fibrous, swellable, or tissue-ingrowth material, the members can trap blood, encourage clot formation or tissue incorporation, and improve the seal over time.

Thus, the two members provide conformability, redundancy, and broader sealing coverage, directing blood through the prosthetic valve rather than around its cuff.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical summary of an implantable heart valve that permits antegrade flow, blocks retrograde flow, and uses directionally oriented seals around the stent’s abluminal surface.
counterfactuals.output:
### Technical Summary

The implantable heart valve is a prosthetic valve assembly configured to permit antegrade blood flow while substantially preventing retrograde flow. The assembly includes a radially expandable stent frame supporting one or more flexible valve leaflets. During forward-pressure conditions, the leaflets open to define an antegrade flow path through the stent lumen. When the pressure gradient reverses, the leaflets coapt to occlude the lumen and inhibit regurgitant flow.

One or more directionally oriented seals are disposed around the stent’s abluminal surface. The seals may comprise flexible skirts, flaps, cuffs, fins, or overlapping membrane elements oriented to respond asymmetrically to blood-flow direction and pressure. During antegrade flow, the seals remain relatively collapsed against the stent or otherwise present low flow resistance. Under retrograde pressure, the seals expand, deflect, or press radially outward against surrounding native tissue, thereby closing gaps between the stent and the implantation site and reducing paravalvular leakage.

The directional seals may extend continuously or intermittently around the stent circumference and may be arranged in one or more axial rows. Their geometry, material stiffness, and attachment orientation can be selected to promote low-profile delivery, secure tissue apposition after deployment, and pressure-responsive sealing. The prosthesis may be configured for transcatheter delivery using a self-expanding or balloon-expandable frame and may be implanted within a native valve annulus, a surgical prosthesis, or another cardiovascular conduit.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a concise invention description for a collapsible tubular stent with prosthetic valve elements and outwardly billowing blood-flow-activated sealing members.
counterfactuals.output: A collapsible prosthetic heart valve includes an expandable tubular stent supporting flexible valve leaflets that regulate unidirectional blood flow. One or more compliant sealing members are disposed around the stent and configured to billow outward under blood-flow pressure after deployment. The billowing members conform to irregularities in the native annulus, thereby sealing paravalvular gaps, reducing leakage, and improving anchoring while maintaining a low delivery profile in the collapsed state.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
